title: Dasher Analytics Event Schema v1
description: Published openly at https://github.com/dasher-project/Dasher-GTK. If it's not in this schema, it's not collected. All Dasher frontends (Windows, Apple, GTK) share the same PostHog project — events are distinguished by the default properties below.

default_properties.description: Automatically appended to every event from every frontend

platform.description: GTK is multiplatform: host OS at compile time (linux on Linux builds, macos on macOS, windows on Windows).

$os.description: The raw HTTP transport sends no SDK context, so $os is set explicitly — keeps OS breakdowns consistent with the Apple/Android SDKs.

$geoip_disable.description: Sent on every event (including crashes): PostHog Cloud must not derive location from the client IP (RFC 0001: no location data).

input_method_changed.note: Not emitted by Dasher-GTK as of 0.2.2; kept here because this schema is shared across frontends.

analytics_id_reset.description: User reset their anonymous analytics ID

settings_reset_defaults.description: User reset every engine parameter to its built-in default

crash.description: Uncaught C++ exception or fatal signal (SIGSEGV/SIGABRT/SIGILL), reported on the launch after the crash.

stack_trace.note: PII-scrubbed; may contain file paths but not user text. Empty for native signals, which are captured async-signal-safe.

crash.note: Dasher-GTK transmits this as a PostHog `$exception` event (Error Tracking), not a custom event named `crash`.

engine_error.description: DasherCore raised its sticky error flag (RFC 0009 A2). Non-fatal: reported once per session and the app keeps running.

stack_trace.note: Fixed marker string identifying the flag, not a captured stack

engine_error.note: Shares the PostHog `$exception` channel with `crash`; the two are distinguished by exception_type.

explicitly_not_collected: User name, email, or account info
